questions.question: Vapour pressure of a liquid

options.text: does not depend upon the nature of the liquid

questions.solution:
**__Concept:__**

**Vapour Pressure**-

__
 
• The pressure at which **liquid and vapour can co exist** at a given temperature is called the **vapour pressure** of the liquid.
 
• When a liquid is kept in a closed vessel with some free space, it starts to **vaporise.**
 
• The vapourisation continues until a state of **equillibrium** is reached between **vapourisation** and** condensation**.
 
• At equilibrium, the state gets saturated and the pressure exerted by the **vapour molecules is called vapour pressure**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/d399fd029edfa7dce4716ae09b95a17b23e0f1110c4a6edf536df99975d7000a.png] 

**Explanation:__**

__
 
• Vapourisation takes place from the **surface** of the liquid.
 
• Two processes are occurring here simultaneously
 
 
• **condensation** of the vapour molecules back to the liquid surface. 
 
• **vapourisation** from the liquid surface.
 
 
 
• To overcome the **forces of attraction** in the surface of the liquids, sufficient **energy of activation** and **kinetic energy **s required.
 
• Energy is also required to go from the l**iquid phase to the vapour phase**. 
 
• Increasing the temperature will increase the **kinetic energy** of the molecules.
 
• This will give them **more energy** to overcome the **attractive forces**
 
• Now, greater number of molecules will go into the **vapour phase**.

Thus, overall **vapour pressure** would i**ncrease with increase of temperature.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] Important Points__**

 
• The vapour pressure does not depend on the free space given or the quantity of liquid.

questions.question: ______ is something that has mass and occupies space.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Matter**____.__

__**Explanation:**__

__
 
• Matter is made up of small particles.
 
• Matter is defined as anything that occupies space and has a definite mass.__
 
• **All matter is composed of atoms and molecules.**
 
• Matter requires at least one subatomic particle, although the most matter is made up of atoms.
 
• The matter around us exists in three states— solid, liquid, and gas.
 
• Solid matter:
 __
 
• Solid matter is made up of tightly packed particles.
 
• A solid can keep its shape because the particles are not free to move but can vibrate in fixed positions.
 
 
 
• Liquid matter:
 
 
• Liquid matter is made up of particles that are loosely packed.
 
• It has no shape and thus takes the shape of the container in which it is kept.
 
• Particles can move freely within a liquid, but they are densely packed, which is why they have a constant volume.
 
 
 
• Gaseous matter:
 
 
• Gaseous matter is made up of very loosely packed particles.
 
• It does not have a specific shape or volume.
 
 

Thus, **Matter is something that has mass and occupies space.**__

questions.question: Which of the following is a homogeneous mixture?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__Su__gar in water**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **__Important Points__**

 
• Sugar in water is a homogeneous mixture.
 
• A** Heterogeneous mixture** has **different proportions of its compound **in a sample.
 
• A **Homogeneous mixture** has the **same proportions of its compound **in a sample.
 
• A Mixture in which solute particle does not dissolve, but get suspended is a suspension.
 
• A solution in which the substances are regularly suspended in a fluid is a Colloidal Solution.
 
• A true solution is a homogeneous mixture of two or more substances in which the substance dissolved in the solvent has a particle size of less than 10-9 m or 1 nm.

questions.question: The boiling point of water is:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**100°C**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The boiling point of water is 100°C.
 
• At sea level, **vapour pressure is equal to the atmospheric pressure at 100 ˚C, **and so this is the temperature** **at which water boils.
 
• Due to this, the temperature required to reach the necessary vapour becomes lower and lower as we get higher above sea level, and the liquid will therefore boil at a lower temperature.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Water is an inorganic, transparent, tasteless, odorless, and nearly colorless chemical substance, which is the main constituent of Earth's hydrosphere and the fluids of all known living organisms. 
 
• It is vital for all known forms of life, even though it provides no calories or organic nutrients.
 
• For water, the vapour pressure reaches the standard atmospheric pressure of 1 atmosphere at 100°C.
 
• So the normal **boiling point of water is 100°C (212°F or 373K).** The boiling point of pure water increases on the addition of soluble substances such as sugar or common salt.

questions.question: The method of separating two liquids based on boiling points
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__Distillation__**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Distillation**, or **classical distillation**, is the process of **separating the components or substances** from a **liquid** mixture by using **selective boiling and condensation.**
 
• **Dry distillation** is the heating of **solid materials to produce gaseous products. **
 
• **Examples of uses of distillation include **purification of alcohol, desalination, crude oil refining, and making liquefied gases from the air. 
 
• **Vacuum distillation** is distillation performed under **reduced pressure**, which allows the **purification of compounds** not readily distilled at **ambient pressures** or simply to save time or energy. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Filtration **is a process used to separate solids from liquids or gases using a filter medium that allows the fluid to pass through but not the solid. 
 
• **Evaporation** is a type of vaporization that occurs on the surface of a liquid as it changes into the gas phase.
 
• **Condensation **is the change of the physical state of matter from the gas phase into the liquid phase and is the reverse of vaporization.

questions.question: What is sublimation?

options.text: direct change of a substance from a gas to a liquid state
direct change of a substance from a gas to a solid state
direct change of a substance from a liquid to a gas state
direct change of a substance from a solid to a gas state

questions.solution:
The correct answer is the __**direct change of a substance from a solid to a gas state.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Sublimation** is a process in which a **solid transforms directly into vapours without changing into liquid.**
 
• This phenomenon can be seen in **camphor or naphthalene balls.**
 
• In the process **snow or ice transforms directly into water vapour without becoming water.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__ **

 
• **Deposition** - It is the process of conversion of a gas to a solid.
 
• Evaporation - It is the process of conversion of a liquid into gas.
 
• Fusion/Melting - It is the process of conversion of a solid into a liquid.
 
• Condensation - It is the process of conversion of a gas into a liquid.
